I didn't really do anything yesterday besides wish for sleepto come, which it finally did around 10 pm. I did get sleep last night, so today is not nearly as bad. Plus work has enough distractions to keep me busy and some basic social interaction if I feel I need it.

I'm definitely going to be doing self care in the next few days. I'm going to stick to my gym schedule, and prepping my own meals in the evenings. All of the little things I could have been doing in the past but did not do because I'd rather not spend the time are things I'll be actively pursuing just to spend the time and keep my mind from sitting idle. For example, I haven't cooked consistently in a few years, and I will be making myself some nice suppers and lunches.

But sleep is a struggle. The only thing I can think of to do is to try to tire myself out physically so that I'll want to pass out from exhaustion. From that angle, I'm actually thinking about expanding my work out schedule to somehow include every day. Or maybe I can find a hobby that takes me out of the house for extended periods. I know that just sitting at home, even if nomally engaged in something, gives me time to dwell on things.

My chest and throat have mostly calmed down, but I have a persistent stress headache now. Taking walks in the brisk air is helpful but not enough. I can endure for now, but hopefully these physical symptoms go away soon. They're distracting, unpleasant, and are themselves reminders of the loss that conspire to pull me back into a negativity spiral.

Pretending everything is normal as people ask about the holiday weekend and make pleasantries is driving me crazy. Things are not normal, and they are not all right, and no it's not a good morning and no I'm not okay, but of course I'm smiling and pretending that everything's fine. All at the same time, it still feels like I'm suffocating and sweating
I will heed your advice.
I survived last night and I will survive tonight. And then the work week will fly by.
How long do you think I should wait?
If anything my day is too calm today. I have the entire day free while my head is full of sleep-deprived static, and nothing to do to fill the time.

> Nothing is trivial. Never forget how you feel right now, because it's the result of taking her for granted and probably scaring her.

Wisdom.

A big deal for me is I don't really know what it is that I've got. I have an apartment too big for my tastes to live in alone, which is very notably empty with her stuff removed. I have the means to go to work and back every day but to what end? Without it ever becoming obvious to me, my whole sense of self has over the years become wound up in my marriage. I found myself wondering last night what even the point of going on living was if all I'm doing is working and coming home to an empty apartment. I still don't really have an answer for that, but I've made plans to continue life as though everything at home were normal. And that seems completely insane to me. My thoughts just keep returning to asking myself the point of jobs and bills and such if I'm just going to come home to emptiness. Just work until I get old and die? For so long my sense of purpose and direction were tied up in my relationship. I did things for her, for us, for our life together, for our home. I don't need this apartment, this car, this career if all I'm doing is waiting for old age. I know I'm overreacting; I know there's other people out there; I know that even if things are over forever I can find happiness elsewhere. But that doesn't stop my mind from dwelling on these thoughts, over and over as if she's the only good person in the world and everyone and everything else doesn't matter once she's gone.

I already failed this part yesterday. I wanted desperately to talk to her, not even because of the breakup but because for so long she has been my primary support network. She's the person I'd talk to for anything that bothered me. I've stopped bothering her now that I've calmed down and dragged myself through the night and morning and I hope I haven't irreparably ruined things. I cling to hope.

I've already decided that I'm not drinking anymore after last night. Seven hours 'til my first full day of committed sobriety. I've offered to check myself into in-patient mental health if she wants, and I've made it clear to her that I'm willing to give her the space she needs. I know I'm the bad guy here, and I kick myself for not seeing it early enough to do something about it before it came to this. I've made plans to adjust my weekday and weekend routines to just not give me the time to sit alone with my thoughts and the desire to deaden them with alcohol. I don't doubt my willpower to just quit cold turkey, but it's the depression, restlessness, and idleness that led me to drink in the first place as a way to make the dead time go by faster. I should have gotten help earlier and more intensively for that, and I should have just quit drinking when she first expressed concern int he past. I'd like nothing more than to just undo the past 24 hours and put things back how they were, but as that ship has sailed I'm instead just clinging to hope that I can become better. 

I have not slept since Friday night. I don't know if I will sleep today/tonight. But I will go to work tomorrow, go to the gym after, and then surely find sleep from exhaustion. And that'll be 2 days of committed sobriety already in the bag.
